# harmoniq_host_app (Resource)

A host app: the application that loads remote modules. Its environments are `harmoniq_environment` resources. Deleting it is refused while any of its environments serves module versions, and for the workspace's default host app while others remain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "harmoniq_host_app" "storefront" {
  workspace            = harmoniq_workspace.checkout_team.slug
  slug                 = "storefront"
  name                 = "Storefront"
  preview_url_template = "https://preview.acme.dev/?harmoniq-env={environment}"
  shared_dependencies = {
    react     = "^19.0.0"
    react-dom = "^19.0.0"
  }
  strict_exposes = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.
- `slug` (String) Host app slug; part of manifest URLs.
- `workspace` (String) Workspace slug.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description.
- `preview_url_template` (String) Preview link for environments, containing `{environment}`, e.g. `https://staging.acme.dev/?harmoniq-env={environment}`.
- `shared_dependencies` (Map of String) Packages the host shares with every module, as semver ranges (`{ react = "^19.0.0" }`). Deploys with conflicting ranges are refused.
- `strict_exposes` (Boolean) Refuse deploys that drop an exposed module the active version had.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `workspace/slug`.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the workspace's default host app (the first one created).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import harmoniq_host_app.storefront checkout-team/storefront
```
